subject: Recap: FinLytics discovery — latency, streaming UX & scaling needs
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Maya Shah <maya@finlytics.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: quick recap & next steps from today’s discovery

Hi Maya — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we captured the priorities correctly and to align on next steps. Note: I attached a short benchmark summary and a draft POC plan for your review.

Pain points we heard
- p95 tail latency spikes during batch-of-live-stream ing workflows (spikes to 900–1,200ms under load) that degrade your real-time UX.
- High per-token cost when you attempt concurrency > 20 simultaneous streams; current infra has poor batching / KV caching so requests are hitting full compute every time.
- Streaming UI experiences sometimes drop partial tokens or delay start-of-stream which your product team flagged as a critical UX regressor.

Current stack (as we heard it)
- Frontend: React streaming client with SSE fallback
- Backend: Kubernetes on GCP (n1-standard class), in-house serving with CPU-based batching; GPU usage limited to offline jobs
- Model: running an open Llama-3 variant (private fork) with float32; limited quantization due to accuracy concerns

Success criteria you called out
- p95 generation latency <= 350ms for requests <= 512 tokens under target concurrency
- Sustained 100 concurrent streaming sessions with start-of-stream latency < 200ms and <1% dropped partial token events
- Unit token cost reduction of 30% vs current infra for a 6-month forecast window

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) Schedule 60m technical demo + throughput review (see suggested times below).
2) Redwood to run a short lab benchmark (controlled replay of your traces) to produce p95 numbers and a configuration recommendation (we'll need a 1–2 hour trace file).
3) If benchmarks look good, plan a 4-week POC using our Dedicated pool or Private deployment depending on your procurement needs — draft POC plan attached.

Suggested demo slots (PST): Wed 2026-05-13 10:00, Wed 2026-05-13 14:00, Thu 2026-05-14 09:00. Please tell us which works or propose alternatives.

What we need from you to run the benchmark
- Representative request traces (1–2 hours, anonymized) or synthetic profile showing tokens per second and average sequence length.
- Target concurrency profile (spikes vs sustained).
- Any non-negotiable security controls (e.g., VPC-only, strict KMS).

I’ll loop in Vanessa and Neha to set up the lab run and schedule the demo.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood-p95-benchmark-summary.xlsx (summary of recent similar customer runs)
- MAL-POC-plan.pdf (draft POC scope and acceptance criteria)

From: Maya Shah <maya@finlytics.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 17:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: quick recap & next steps from today’s discovery

Hi Sergio — thanks for the clear summary. This matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- The p95 spikes we reported are specifically for interactive query sessions when multiple users trigger streaming completions (typical request length ~ 200–400 tokens). We see the 900–1,200ms p95 most often during business-hours bursts (09:30–11:30 ET).
- Concurrency target: 100 sustained concurrent interactive sessions with headroom to 150 for peak events.
- Start-of-stream issues: our UI shows a blank spinner for ~300–500ms before tokens arrive on some sessions; that's causing a bad retention signal.
- Security: Procurement will require SOC 2 Type II evidence and a data retention policy that lets us delete traces after 30 days. VPC peering is preferred but not mandatory for POC.

We can provide a 2-hour anonymized trace (will scrub PII) and a short doc that describes our concurrency curve. I can upload both to the Drive link you provided — will do by EOD tomorrow.

For demo time, Wed 2026-05-13 14:00 PST works for me. Please invite any SEs who will cover the throughput benchmarks and streaming optimizations.

Thanks,
Maya
Head of Product | FinLytics
maya@finlytics.com | +1 212-555-0888

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: FinLytics next steps (prep + SE ask)

Looping in a quick plan for prep before the 14:00 demo (Sergio booked). Notes:
- Ask Solutions Eng (R&D) to bring a short demo of prefix/KV cache behavior on streaming workloads and a GPU-backed config that hits p95 <= 350ms for 512 tokens.
- Neha: please prep a SOC 2 evidence packet + our data retention matrix and confirm whether we can sign the 30-day deletion clause for the POC.
- Sergio: get the anonymized trace and concurrency curve from Maya; upload to the secure lab bucket. We'll run an initial replay overnight and aim to share bench numbers by Thu morning.

Keep this tight — FinLytics looks time-sensitive and procurement is likely to move quickly if benchmarks are clean.

V.

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, East | Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Maya Shah <maya@finlytics.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Confirmed: Demo 2026-05-13 14:00 PST + what we’ll deliver by Thu

Hi Maya — great, confirmed for Wed 2026-05-13 14:00 PST (calendar invite sent). Quick note on what you’ll see and what we’ll deliver by Thu morning after the demo:

Demo agenda (60m):
- 10m: quick goals alignment and success criteria (you + Arjun)
- 20m: SE walkthrough of streaming optimizations (prefix/KV caching, batching strategy)
- 20m: live replay of a short segment of your trace and initial p95 numbers (we'll use anonymized data)
- 10m: Q&A + procurement ask list

Deliverables by Thu EOD (post-demo):
- Lab replay report with p50/p95/p99 for your trace under three configurations (hosted baseline, GPU-optimized, quantized profile) — expectations: target p95 <= 350ms on the GPU-optimized config for <=512 tokens.
- Draft POC scope with timeline and acceptance criteria (we attached a starter already).
- SOC 2 evidence packet and data-retention confirmation from Neha.

What we need from you before demo: upload the anonymous trace and concurrency doc to https://drive.redwood.com/FinLytics/Discovery-Notes-20260512 or reply with a secure S3 link. Also let us know if there are any additional stakeholders to add.

Thanks for the speedy turnaround — we’ll aim to have the lab numbers ready quickly so procurement has something concrete to evaluate.

Best,
Sergio

Attachment reference: MAL-POC-plan.pdf (draft)
